:::{#thm-contrapositive}
#### A conditional is equivalent to its contrapositive

For any propositions $P$ and $Q$,

$$
(P \Rightarrow Q) \equiv (\neg Q \Rightarrow \neg P).
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

By the definition of [implies](#def-implies),
$P \Rightarrow Q$ is false exactly when $P$ is true and $Q$ is false.
By the same definition,
$\neg Q \Rightarrow \neg P$ is false exactly when $\neg Q$ is true and $\neg P$ is false,
that is, exactly when $Q$ is false and $P$ is true.
So the two propositions are false in the same row of a truth table
and true in the other three,
which is @def-logically-equivalent.

:::

:::
